question.text: Chapter 9 distinguishes Angel vs VC at the metric level. An Angel looks at team + CAC/CLV; a VC additionally looks at which revenue-consistency metric?

answer.text: Monthly Run Rate (MRR) or Annual Run Rate (ARR) — to gauge consistency and sustainability of revenue.

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 9 says: 'Venture capital investors look at metrics like Monthly Run Rate (MRR) or Annual Run Rate (ARR), to gauge the consistency and sustainability of revenue generated by the investee companies.' ARR = MRR × 12 and shows predictable revenue visibility. The Trap: Option B (EBITDA/DSCR) is a PE/debt-fund metric for mature businesses. Option C (EV/BV) is a banking-sector valuation measure. Option D (Altman Z) is a bankruptcy-prediction score for distressed investing, not growth-stage VC. Cross-Exam Context: XV (Research Analyst) uses ARR heavily in SaaS research. XIX-A uses it in product marketing disclosure. Cat III Managers (XIX-E, not yet tested) rarely use ARR — hedge strategies use listed-market metrics like beta, Sharpe, drawdown. Manager's Pro-Tip: Insist on a 'committed ARR' definition in the term sheet — exclude trial users, free tiers, and reversible contracts. Mark-to-cash ARR (collected revenue / 12) avoids over-optimistic valuations that hurt LP IRR at exit.
